facility_roles.note: Start per the collaboration paper (transfer initiated early 2012; underground assembly February 2013). End 2020 is the upper bound for the end of dual-phase data taking (UCLA DM 2020 abstract); the hardware stays at LSC for DArTinArDM. The detector sits in Hall A of LSC (arXiv:1307.0117, Sec. 2.1.3).
facility_roles.quote: In early 2012 the transfer to its final place in the underground laboratory of Canfranc (LSC) was initiated with the installation of the vessel and the majority of the cryogenic parts.

intervals.label: approved as LSC EXP-08-2010 / CERN RE18

intervals.quote: Developed at CERN as Recognized Experiment RE18, the experiment has been approved in 2010 to be installed in the Spanish underground site LSC (Laboratorio Subterraneo de Canfranc).

intervals.label: construction and surface tests at CERN, transfer to and assembly at LSC
intervals.note: Start of construction is not published in the sources read (design paper hep-ph/0510320 is of October 2005; the 1-ton detector was 'under construction and commissioning on surface at CERN' in December 2009, arXiv:0912.2962). End = first data taking at LSC (April 2013); the underground assembly was completed in February 2013 (arXiv:1307.0117, Sec. 2.1.3).
intervals.quote: It was constructed and operated at CERN [3, 4].

intervals.label: underground commissioning with gas argon, then liquid-argon filling
intervals.note: End: filling of the vessel with nearly 2 t of liquid argon was completed in February 2015 (arXiv:1505.02443, Sec. 1).
intervals.quote: First data taking at LSC was carried out for two weeks in April 2013

intervals.label: liquid-argon data taking (single-phase Run I in 2015, later dual-phase run)
intervals.note: Start per the collaboration's report ('first period of physics data taking in the single-phase operation mode'); the 2016-2018 papers call the same 2015 run a 'commissioning run'. End year (2020) is only an upper bound taken from the UCLA DM 2020 abstract ('has recently finished data taking in dual-phase mode', conference of 25-28 March 2020); the exact end is not published in the sources read.
intervals.quote: Now the project has entered the first period of physics data taking in the single-phase operation mode (ArDM Run I).

intervals.label: ArDM Run I (single phase, liquid argon)
intervals.note: End year from 'completed a single-phase commissioning run in 2015' (arXiv:1712.01932, abstract); the report of May 2015 planned data taking 'through June 2015'.
intervals.quote: Now the project has entered the first period of physics data taking in the single-phase operation mode (ArDM Run I).

intervals.label: dual-phase run (Run II)
intervals.note: Start unknown: the December 2017 paper only says the results 'pave the way for the next physics run of ArDM in the double-phase operational mode' (arXiv:1712.01932). End is an upper bound (abstract for a conference scheduled 25-28 March 2020).
intervals.quote: The ArDM experiment, a tonne-scale dual-phase liquid Argon TPC, has recently finished data taking in dual-phase mode.

intervals.label: completed (dual-phase data taking ended; hardware reused for DArTinArDM)
intervals.note: Year is an upper bound (abstract written before the 25-28 March 2020 conference). The LSC page for DArTinArDM (Exp-13-2019) calls it 'El antiguo detector ArDM' (the former ArDM detector) and says the dual-phase configuration remains installed; DArT is a 39Ar assay inside the ArDM vessel, not a dark matter search (excluded as a separate experiment, see the log).

notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
No official ArDM website was found; website left null.
Surface phase: built and operated at CERN as Recognised Experiment RE18 (arXiv:0912.2962, arXiv:1307.0117); facility:cern is recorded as prototype_host.

Status 'completed' rests on the UCLA DM 2020 abstract ('has recently finished data taking in dual-phase mode'; conference cancelled, abstract page read) and the LSC page calling it 'El antiguo detector ArDM'. The exact end of data taking, the start of the dual-phase run and the decommissioning date are not published in the sources read.

The ArDM vessel is being reused for DArTinArDM (LSC Exp-13-2019, arXiv:2001.08106; arXiv:2609.39400 of September 2026 says the project 'is being commissioned'): a 39Ar assay chamber inside the ArDM LAr bath, not a dark matter search, therefore not recorded as an experiment here.
No WIMP-search result of ArDM was found in the sources read; the dual-phase analysis was 'in preparation' at the time of the 2020 abstract.

summary.plain: ArDM was a ton-scale liquid argon detector built at CERN, then installed in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees, to search for WIMP dark matter. It took liquid-argon data from 2015 and finished dual-phase running by about 2020. Its papers report detector performance and backgrounds, not a WIMP limit.
summary.technical: Double-phase liquid argon TPC (scintillation S1 plus ionisation S2 read out through PMT arrays) with an 850 kg active target in a vessel filled with nearly 2 t of LAr; installed in Hall A of LSC (about 2500 m w.e.) in 2013. Run I (2015) was single phase: attenuation length of the argon scintillation light close to 0.5 m, 39Ar activity and Rn-222 emanation measured, and a pulse-shape rejection power for electron recoils above 10^8 estimated with a Cf-252 source (50% nuclear-recoil acceptance, >50 photons). A dual-phase run finished by early 2020. The cryostat is reused by DArTinArDM (Exp-13-2019).
